At repo_ref, plan.mjs line 880 prints `archive requires a closing pull request merged into <nameWithOwner>:<branch>`, and plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/references/plan-contract.md says at line 196 that its refusal stderr strings are exact and lists the old text at line 218. plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/AGENTS.md lines 59-66 make plan-contract.md canonical, tell authors to coordinate edits when concepts change, and say that no test pins skill prose, so the gate does not catch the drift. No Files cell of steps 1 to 4 names plan-contract.md, so after step 1 the canonical contract lists a refusal that plan.mjs no longer prints and does not list the one it prints. Step 1 must also update plan-contract.md line 218 (step 4 already holds the plan-manager/SKILL.md content-hash refresh), or keep the old refusal text.

known.title: Acceptance A5 greps plan.mjs for viewer.login, which already matches viewer{login} in the snapshot query, so it passes without step 2
known.locator: Acceptance, row A5 (line 39); Steps, row 2 login_error (line 27)
known.summary: A5 runs `grep -q 'viewer.login'` on plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/scripts/plan.mjs and expects exit 0, as the check that ACTING_LOGIN_ERROR names the GraphQL viewer.login lookup (goal item 2, step 2). The pattern is a basic regular expression, and the GNU grep manual (https://www.gnu.org/software/grep/manual/html_node/Fundamental-Structure.html) says 'The period ‘.’ matches any single character.' At repo_ref, plan.mjs line 168 already holds `viewer{login}` in the readSnapshot query, so the command exits 0 before any change (checked with GNU grep 3.12), while ACTING_LOGIN_ERROR at line 18 still names `gh api user --jq .login`. A5 passes when step 2 is not done, so it proves nothing about the new message; it must check the ACTING_LOGIN_ERROR line itself, for example with a fixed-string match of the new text on that constant.

known.title: Research lets step 1 accept one keyword before a comma-separated issue list, so whether archive accepts such a description is the implementer's choice, and one choice accepts a closer without a valid closing keyword
known.locator: Research, hasClosingKeyword bullet (line 17); Steps, row 1 separator (line 26)
known.summary: The Research bullet on hasClosingKeyword says that step 1 may also let one keyword cover a comma-separated list such as `Fixes #4, #5` if the regex stays readable, so the result of archive for such a description is left to the implementer. At repo_ref, hasClosingKeyword (plan.mjs lines 122-128) needs the issue reference right after the keyword and its separator, so it refuses `Fixes #4, #5` for issue 5; the list option makes archive exit 0 for the same plan. No Acceptance row or listed test case fixes the result. GitHub documents (https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/using-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue) the multiple-issue syntax as 'Use full syntax for each issue' (`Resolves #10, resolves #123, ...`), so `Fixes #4, #5` is no closing keyword for #5, and the same page says that a pull request or branch can be linked to an issue to close it on merge, without a keyword. plan-contract.md at repo_ref (lines 245-248) makes the closing keyword in the description the proof and says that a merely linked pull request is not proof. With the list option, archive accepts a linked closer whose description has no valid keyword for the plan. The plan must decide to refuse the list form and add a refusal case for it.

known.title: Research says that archive runs hasClosingKeyword on the associated pull requests of a commit closer, but the commit path has no keyword check, so the commit-closer refusal cases of step 1 cannot pass
known.locator: Research, refusal-cases bullet (line 18); Steps, row 1 separator (line 26); Do not touch, item 1 (line 43)
known.summary: The Research bullet on the refusal cases says that commit closers reach the same check because archive runs hasClosingKeyword on the description of each associated pull request, and step 1 adds the line-break refusal cases also for a commit closer. At repo_ref this is false: archivePlan (plan.mjs lines 863-871) calls hasClosingKeyword only for a PullRequest closer and takes issue.associatedPullRequests of a Commit closer with no keyword check, and the associated pull requests are read with PULL_REQUEST_FIELDS (line 20, through PULL_REQUEST_CONNECTION at line 21, CLOSED_EVENT_FIELDS at line 74, and associatedNodes at line 143), which has no body field. plan-contract.md at repo_ref (lines 244-247) also accepts a commit associated with a merged pull request and asks the closing keyword only of a pull-request closer, and scripts/tests/plan-cli.mjs lines 521-550 already archive a commit closer whose associated pull request has `body: null`. So the new commit-closer refusal cases archive with exit 0, step 1 Done when, A2 (line 36), and A4 (line 38) fail, and a pass needs a change to the commit-closer proof, which Do not touch (line 43) excludes. The commit-closer cases must go, or the plan must change the commit-closer proof on purpose.
